title: POC Weekly Caching Sync - Prefix & KV Hit Rate Review
summary: Weekly POC sync to review prefix/KV cache hit rates and discuss prompt reuse strategy. SE presented recent metrics (overall hit rate ~28%), proposed canonicalization steps and TTL adjustments. Action items: run 100k synthetic benchmark with normalized prompts, provide config snippet for cache keys, and schedule a deep dive on pre-warming and KV shard sizing next week.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-08-05
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Sarah Patel (Nimbus Head of ML), Raj Mehta (Nimbus Platform Eng), Lina Gomez (Nimbus CTO)

Summary: Quick sync on caching work — looked at prefix/KV hit rates, prompt reuse strategy, and next steps to improve hit rate and reduce cost.

00:00:00 - Maya Chen: thanks everybody for joining, um quick agenda, metrics, tuning options, next steps.
00:00:25 - Sarah Patel: yep thanks maya, we've been seeing low cache hit rate so was hoping you could walk through what you saw last week.
00:00:42 - Jordan Lee: sure, i pulled the numbers — across the pilot traffic our KV/prefix cache hit is about 28% overall, but it's very route dependent, top-3 routes see ~45-50% and a long tail at single-digit hits.
00:01:05 - Raj Mehta: that jives with what we saw; some routes have tons of prompt variants, different user metadata injected.
00:01:18 - Lina Gomez: curious, is 28% surprising? what's reasonable?
00:01:27 - Jordan Lee: reasonable target for this workload is 55-65% with canonicalization + template reuse, TTL tuning and grouping similar prompts. right now the main issues are prompt-level variance and long literal prefixes.
00:01:50 - Sarah Patel: can you show an example?
00:01:55 - Jordan Lee: yeah, e g we saw the onboarding flow — the system prompt has user_name, locale, tiny timestamps — those cause distinct cache keys. if we canonicalize the system prompt (replace user_name with token, remove ephemeral timestamps) hit rate jumps.
00:02:18 - Maya Chen: and to be clear, we're talking prefix cache and KV cache; prefix cache handles deterministic common prefixes (like system + few-shot templates) while KV caches final token states for reuse across sessions. both can be helped by prompt normalization.
00:02:40 - Raj Mehta: what about TTL? we currently set TTL 30s for KV entries to cap memory.
00:02:49 - Jordan Lee: 30s is conservative; for many of your routes traffic bursts are spaced, we can try 60-120s for hot routes and evict cold keys quicker. also size-based eviction with LRU helps.
00:03:10 - Sarah Patel: any risk with longer TTLs for privacy/compliance?
00:03:15 - Maya Chen: good question — TTL doesn't change retention in logs/audit; you control persistent logs and KMS. from a privacy standpoint we can mask PII before caching or mark keys as non-cacheable. we documented options in the security pack — happy to share.
00:03:37 - Lina Gomez: also interested in encryption at rest for cached payloads — are keys encrypted in all deployments?
00:03:44 - Jordan Lee: yes, in dedicated/private mode we use customer-managed KMS/HSM options. hosted has server-side encryption and optional bring-your-own-key for private.
00:03:58 - Raj Mehta: back to hit rate, you mentioned prompt templates — is there automated canonicalization in Redwood today?
00:04:06 - Jordan Lee: we have heuristics in runtime that normalizes whitespace and strips timestamps, but not domain-aware canonicalization. for this POC we can add a small layer that applies route-specific canonicalizers — e g drop user_name, map currencies to canonical symbol.
00:04:28 - Sarah Patel: would that be user-configurable? we can't whitelist everything centrally.
00:04:33 - Jordan Lee: yes, route-level rules you push as JSON config; SE can produce samples.
00:04:40 - Maya Chen: quick note on metrics: Jordan ran sample test last week with 25k calls — details are in the sheet — overall 28% but if you apply canonicalization heuristics to top-5 routes, hit rate increases to ~52% for those routes.
00:04:59 - Sarah Patel: ok that feels promising. what's next to prove it in our traffic?
00:05:06 - Jordan Lee: we recommend a synthetic 100k run using sanitized traffic and canonicalization rules. that gives stable hit-rate estimates per route and lets us tune TTL and shard sizing.
00:05:21 - Raj Mehta: can you run that on our dedicated pool or will it use hosted?
00:05:27 - Maya Chen: we can run on dedicated if you give us test creds, but usually we run on an isolated Redwood environment to avoid impacting production. outcome is the same.
00:05:36 - Lina Gomez: what about latency impact from canonicalization? any added ms?
00:05:41 - Jordan Lee: microseconds to low ms, negligible compared to perf gains from hits. biggest latency wins come from prefix hits where we avoid full decoder steps.
00:05:55 - Sarah Patel: do we have cost modeling? if we increase TTL, memory cost goes up, but token cost drops.
00:06:03 - Jordan Lee: yes, we have a cost model: token cost saved per cache hit minus memory overhead. Jordan (SE) will share a simple spreadsheet.
00:06:13 - Maya Chen: action items we'll capture.
00:06:18 - 00:06:25 - [brief cross talk about calendar invites]
00:06:30 - Jordan Lee: another observation — many prompts differ only by trailing system notes like "-- browser: chrome" or session ids. trimming those before keying gives immediate wins.
00:06:46 - Raj Mehta: that's easy to do on our side in the SDK; we can implement light normalization client-side.
00:06:52 - Sarah Patel: but we'd prefer Redwood to handle it server-side so we don't have to push changes to older apps.
00:06:59 - Maya Chen: we can offer both — SDK normalization and server-side rules in the runtime. choose both for fastest results.
00:07:10 - Jordan Lee: sample config snippet: key = hash(route + canonicalized_prefix + template_version). we recommend explicit template_version to invalidate old templates.
00:07:23 - Lina Gomez: template versioning seems smart — we need a way to bump templates without cold starting all caches.
00:07:29 - Jordan Lee: exactly, bumping template_version invalidates keys gracefully.
00:07:34 - Sarah Patel: question: are we able to pre-warm cache for scheduled flows? e g nightly jobs?
00:07:41 - Jordan Lee: yes — pre-warm via bulk writes to KV or run a warm-up load; we'll discuss shard sizing for that.
00:07:50 - Raj Mehta: how do we pick shard count? we have high concurrency on a few routes.
00:07:56 - Jordan Lee: shard sizing depends on memory per key and throughput — we'll run a profiling job in synthetic run and propose shard counts. usually start with 8-16 shards for this scale, adjust based on p99 latencies.
00:08:11 - Maya Chen: can we see the current distribution?
00:08:14 - Jordan Lee: yes I'll attach the distribution CSV — top key space is 60% from three routes.
00:08:21 - [pause while Jordan references sheet]
00:08:35 - Jordan Lee: some nuance — prefix caching helps when you have identical prefix across different user sessions; it's most effective for templated flows like "account summary" where prompt body is same and only slot values differ.
00:08:50 - Sarah Patel: our biggest cost is the account-summary and transaction-explain flows.
00:08:55 - Jordan Lee: those are great candidates. start there.
00:09:00 - Lina Gomez: are there any security concerns about caching user-specific content?
00:09:05 - Maya Chen: yes — we recommend masking PII and optionally marking keys as non-cacheable; there is also RBAC on cache admin. we'll share the compliance doc.
00:09:16 - Raj Mehta: technical detail — what's the canonical key length? hashing?
00:09:20 - Jordan Lee: we use SHA256 then base64-truncate to 48 chars for index; avoids huge key sizes and still practically collision-free.
00:09:31 - Sarah Patel: ok. next, what's the plan to measure improvement after changes?
00:09:36 - Jordan Lee: metrics: per-route hit rate, hit latency delta, token-savings-per-minute, cost-estimate saved; we'll provide dashboards and raw CSV.
00:09:47 - Maya Chen: timeline — propose canonicalization rules this week, synthetic run next week, deep-dive on shard sizing after results.
00:09:55 - Raj Mehta: sounds good. specific ask — Jordan, can you send the config snippet and the small script to canonicalize locally?
00:10:02 - Jordan Lee: yes I'll push a gist and include inside the support ticket.
00:10:07 - Lina Gomez: do you foresee any functional regressions from canonicalization? e g we lose context?
00:10:12 - Jordan Lee: risk is minimal if you only normalize non-semantic tokens (timestamps, session ids), but if you strip content that changes meaning you can degrade answers. that's why route-level rules are important.
00:10:26 - Sarah Patel: can we A/B test canonicalization?
00:10:29 - Maya Chen: yes we support A/B via rollout policies — run 10% traffic through canonicalization and measure metrics.
00:10:38 - Raj Mehta: we'll likely start with A/B on account-summary.
00:10:42 - Jordan Lee: one more ops tip — add template_version into the cache key so you can rotate templates quickly.
00:10:49 - [10:11 - 00:11:10 omitted short banter about lunches]
00:11:20 - Jordan Lee: okay moving into benchmarks — last week's run details: 25k calls, 28% hit overall, memory footprint ~3.2GB across KV nodes, average saving per hit ~0.6 tokens-equivalent on these routes.
00:11:38 - Sarah Patel: tokens-equivalent? how are you computing that?
00:11:41 - Jordan Lee: we estimate saved decoder steps converted to token-exec cost; sheet has the math.
00:11:48 - Raj Mehta: can we simulate QA style prompts? they vary a lot.
00:11:53 - Jordan Lee: for QA flows canonicalization gains less but still some wins for boilerplate prompts; main wins are templated flows.
00:12:03 - Lina Gomez: ok role question — who will own production rollout?
00:12:07 - Sarah Patel: we'll own rollout on our side but Redwood will provide config, implementation guide and support during ramp.
00:12:15 - Maya Chen: yep we'll provide runbook and on-call window during pilot.
00:12:21 - Jordan Lee: quick sample canonicalization rule — remove / replace regex (session_id:\s*\w+), strip headers starting with "--", normalize dates to <DATE>.
00:12:37 - Raj Mehta: can you post that rule?
00:12:40 - Jordan Lee: will include in gist.
00:12:45 - Sarah Patel: any limits on KV size / key counts we should know?
00:12:49 - Jordan Lee: depends on deployment; hosted limits are documented — for dedicated we can configure cluster size to your needs. we'll propose sizing after synthetic run.
00:13:00 - Lina Gomez: what about cold start penalty after template_version bump?
00:13:05 - Jordan Lee: temporary spike in token cost until cache warms; mitigations: gradual rollout or bulk pre-warm.
00:13:15 - Sarah Patel: ok i want to see pre-warm plan in the next doc.
00:13:18 - Maya Chen: noted.
00:13:22 - Jordan Lee: we're also seeing a few noisy keys that account for 12% of writes — we can blacklist or rate-limit those keys server-side.
00:13:34 - Raj Mehta: blacklist is fine, we'll review pattern.
00:13:38 - Maya Chen: quick re-cap of proposed experiment: 1) apply route-level canonicalization for top-3 routes, 2) run 100k synthetic run with TTL variants, 3) measure per-route hit and cost savings, 4) plan shard sizing and pre-warm.
00:13:58 - Lina Gomez: that aligns.
00:14:02 - Sarah Patel: anything else on observability? we want token-level breakdown.
00:14:08 - Jordan Lee: Redwood Console will show token breakdown by route/model, plus trace IDs and sample payloads (sanitized). we'll share a dashboard link after the run.
00:14:21 - Raj Mehta: do you capture kv hit/miss with trace ids so we can sample misses?
00:14:26 - Jordan Lee: yes each request has trace id and KV hit/miss flag. we'll give you sample rows.
00:14:33 - [short pause]
00:14:45 - Sarah Patel: security doc? send to procurement.
00:14:51 - Maya Chen: will send SOC2/ISO docs and the compliance pack.
00:14:55 - Lina Gomez: any blockers from Redwood side for running synthetic?
00:15:00 - Jordan Lee: need sanitized prompt variants and a test creds or allowlist for the job. otherwise none.
00:15:08 - Raj Mehta: we'll prepare data and scrub PII.
00:15:12 - Sarah Patel: timeline again?
00:15:15 - Maya Chen: send rules by 2025-08-07, customer sample prompt variants by 2025-08-08, run by 2025-08-12, deep dive 2025-08-13.
00:15:25 - Lina Gomez: ok agreed.
00:15:30 - Jordan Lee: any other questions about metrics or tooling?
00:15:34 - Raj Mehta: curious about rollout policies — can we automatically fallback if quality drops?
00:15:39 - Jordan Lee: yes auto-fallback policy exists — you can route to baseline model if canonicalized path underperforms. we can set guardrails on quality metrics.
00:15:51 - Sarah Patel: good.
00:15:54 - Maya Chen: final quick items — Jordan will send gist and sheet; I'll send security docs and a sample runbook.
00:16:04 - Jordan Lee: noted.
00:16:08 - [closing small talk]
00:16:20 - Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the ticket and with the CSV.
00:16:26 - Sarah Patel: thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript (recording stop).

Notes: transcription contains small errors and shorthand; timestamps sampled every ~15-90s to mirror Fireflies style. Referenced assets: "cache-hit-results-2025-08-01.csv" (sheet link), "canonicalization-gist" (Redwood gist link), security pack link (shared in follow-up).
